forecasts.question: Will Iran take a NEW concrete action to fully close the Strait of Hormuz before EOD 2026-06-09?
forecasts.delta_reason: Iran launched multiple drones toward the Strait of Hormuz on 2026-06-06 (NBC News, Washington Post, Times of Israel). US CENTCOM said the drones posed 'immediate threat to regional maritime traffic'; US shot down 4 and struck Iranian coastal surveillance radar sites on Qeshm Island and Goruk. Iran's Mehr news agency described them as 'warning shots near the strait.' This is a new IRGC action in the horizon window. Resolution criteria requires an attack on a commercial vessel or new mine-laying; the drones were intercepted before striking a vessel, so full-YES criteria are not yet met but probability rises materially given 3 days remain and the precedent of escalating IRGC action.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a TIER1 source reports a NEW concrete Iranian closure action between 2026-06-02 and 2026-06-09: fresh mine-laying, a formally declared total-closure/exclusion order, or a new IRGC seizure/attack on a commercial vessel.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Two independent TIER1 OR one TIER1 + a US/UK maritime authority (NAVCENT/UKMTO) advisory.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Repetition of existing warnings or continuation of the pre-existing de facto closure does NOT count; a single unverified state-media claim without corroboration = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. Drones intercepted before hitting a vessel = PARTIAL, not YES.

indicators.name: UKMTO/NAVCENT advisory of new closure action
indicators.expected_effect: +25pp toward YES — NAVCENT struck radar sites after June 6 drone launch, confirming new hostile action

indicators.name: New AIS evidence of mine-laying or IRGC seizure/attack on commercial vessel
indicators.expected_effect: +30pp toward YES — drones launched toward commercial traffic, intercepted; mine-laying not confirmed on June 4-6

forecasts.question: Will Iran and the US publicly confirm a signed written framework before EOD 2026-06-05?
forecasts.delta_reason: Horizon passed EOD 2026-06-05. Iranian FM Araghchi stated on 2026-06-04 that 'there is currently no formal process of negotiations between Iran and the United States' (Tasnim/Bloomberg). No signed framework was publicly confirmed by either principal. Iran's mediator-channel suspension on June 1 was not reversed. RESOLVE-NO.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a named US administration official AND a named Iranian official publicly confirm a signed written framework (by any name); OR if the document text is published by Axios/Reuters/State Dept or Iran MFA with both parties acknowledging authenticity. Verbal 'agreement in principle' does not count.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: At minimum Reuters AND one of Axios/AP/AFP quoting named US AND Iranian principals (not envoys alone). Official Iran MFA statement or State Dept press release also resolves.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Agreement by envoys only without principal confirmation (Trump/Pezeshkian or Mojtaba Khamenei's office) within 72h = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. If Iran signs but Khamenei's office disavows within 72h = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

Iran mediator channel reopened after 1 Jun suspension

forecasts.question: Will Hormuz commercial shipping resume to >=50 daily transits (7-day avg) before EOD 2026-06-10?
forecasts.delta_reason: AIS trackers as of June 5 recorded approximately 10 commercial transits/day versus a 95/day pre-crisis baseline (IMF PortWatch June 5 data, HormuzTracker). With 4 days remaining in the horizon and the Iran-US MOU still unsigned, a recovery from ~10 to >=50 transits/day averaged over 7 consecutive days is physically implausible. Iran's June 6 drone launch against commercial shipping further extends the effective closure. Moved to floor probability 0.05.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if Hormuz Strait Monitor (or UNCTAD, or Lloyd's List) reports >=50 daily transits averaged over 7 consecutive days within the horizon window. NO if average stays below 50/day for the full horizon window.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Hormuz Strait Monitor / IMF PortWatch (primary), Lloyd's List Intelligence (secondary), UNCTAD Maritime Trade quarterly (lagging).
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Dark-fleet/Iranian-flagged-only count with Western insurers still refusing = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. PGSA addendum: third-country vessels under Iran's PGSA toll regime count ONLY IF >=2 of Hormuz Strait Monitor/Lloyd's List/UNCTAD/Windward confirm them independent; PGSA self-reported excluded.

forecasts.question: Will Iran resume negotiations with the US before EOD 2026-06-16?
forecasts.delta_reason: Iranian FM Araghchi stated on 2026-06-04 that 'there is currently no formal process of negotiations between Iran and the United States, but messages are still being exchanged' via mediators (Bloomberg, CBS News). One regional source told CNN that 'talks are back on track' following the June 1 suspension, but Iran's own FM disputed this framing. Iran's June 6 drone launch toward Hormuz and US counter-strikes on Iranian radar sites add new friction to the diplomatic track. The Israel-Lebanon conditional ceasefire announced June 4 (Israel-Lebanon agreed, but Hezbollah rejected it June 4-5) has not yet produced the Lebanon de-escalation Iran requires. Net: message exchange continues but formal resumption not observed; p moved down 5pp.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if an Iranian official or state media (IRNA/Tasnim/Fars) confirms negotiations with the US resumed, OR a named US/mediator (Oman/Qatar) official confirms Iran re-engaged, before EOD 2026-06-16.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Two independent TIER1 OR one TIER1 + official Iranian state-media.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Trump-only assertions without Iranian/mediator confirmation do NOT count; indirect message exchanges that are not negotiations = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

indicators.expected_effect: +25pp toward YES — Araghchi denied formal process as of June 4

forecasts.question: Will Hormuz reach >=50 commercial transits/day (7-day avg) before EOD 2026-07-02?
forecasts.delta_reason: AIS data as of June 5-6 records approximately 10 transits/day; Iran's June 6 drone launch against commercial traffic and ongoing mine presence extend the effective closure timeline. The Iran-US MOU remains unsigned. Iran's FM confirmed on June 4 that 'no formal process of negotiations' exists, while Hezbollah's rejection of the Israel-Lebanon ceasefire removes a key de-escalation condition Iran tied to resuming talks. A 26-day recovery to >=50 transits is less likely than last assessed; moved down 5pp.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if IMF PortWatch (or equivalent AIS) records >=50 commercial transits/day averaged over any consecutive 7-day window between 2026-06-02 and 2026-07-02.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: IMF PortWatch + one TIER1/OSINT shipping report (Bloomberg/Reuters/Lloyd's List).
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Naval-escorted convoys count; one-off surge days below a 7-day window do NOT qualify; if PortWatch unpublished, use best AIS tracker and flag AMBIGUOUS if sources conflict >20%.

forecasts.question: Will the Knesset pass the dissolution bill's final reading with an election date earlier than 2026-10-27 before EOD 2026-07-15?
forecasts.delta_reason: No material movement since June 2 first reading. The dissolution bill passed first reading 106-0 on June 2; the committee established a date range of September 8 to October 20 but did not set a specific date. No second reading has been scheduled as of June 6. Shas and UTJ publicly prefer September while Netanyahu prefers October; deadlock persists.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if the Knesset passes the dissolution bill in final (third) reading specifying an election date earlier than 2026-10-27, before EOD 2026-07-15.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Two TIER1 (Times of Israel/Reuters/AP) citing the Knesset plenum vote record.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Preliminary/first/second readings without final passage do NOT count; if a bill passes but sets a date on/after 27 Oct, resolve NO; if passage occurs but the date is left to a later committee, AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

forecasts.question: Will Hezbollah publicly accept the Israel-Lebanon conditional ceasefire framework before EOD 2026-06-13?
forecasts.delta_reason: New forecast. Israel and Lebanon agreed on June 4 to a conditional ceasefire requiring Hezbollah to cease fire and withdraw from southern Lebanon pilot zones (US-led talks, Euronews, Al Jazeera). Hezbollah leader Naim Kassem on June 4-5 formally rejected the framework, calling it 'surrender' (NPR, Time). Fighting continued after the agreement. However, the ceasefire framework remains on the table with US pressure; there is a small probability Hezbollah changes position under pressure or Iran brokers a modified acceptance before June 13.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a named Hezbollah senior official (secretary-general, political bureau, or Naim Kassem) publicly states acceptance of the Israel-Lebanon ceasefire framework in a form covered by two TIER1 sources, before EOD 2026-06-13.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Two independent TIER1 (Reuters/AP/AFP/Al Jazeera) quoting named Hezbollah official. Hezbollah-affiliated Al-Manar/Al-Mayadeen alone does not resolve.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Partial de-escalation or local pause without formal acceptance of the framework = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. Iran brokering a pause on behalf of Hezbollah without Hezbollah's own statement = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

indicators.name: Kassem or Hezbollah political bureau issues formal acceptance statement
Iran signals to Hezbollah to accept modified framework
